extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural applicants and investigators (PIs, new investigators, K/R awardees, research administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical advice and procedural standards for interpreting eRA/CSR statuses, interacting with Program Officers and GMS, choosing study sections, preparing resubmissions/JIT/rebuttals, and understanding paylines and funding likelihood for NIH grant applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting 'Council review completed' status
rubrics_metrics.description: "This is just a formality to convey that Council has considered your applications." May indicate the application has passed electronic Council; could be considered for funding but actual award decision depends on IC and budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume immediate funding; POs/GMS will not have meaningful funding likelihood until budget is signed. You can ask PO whether to prepare an A1 resubmission for the November cycle, but otherwise wait for JIT or further status changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: eRA status transitions (pending/award processing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statuses can move from 'council review completed' -> 'pending' -> 'awarded', and in some cases change directly to 'awarded' (especially for small awards like R03) if staff are processing many awards at year-end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect administrative variability (delays or skipped intermediary statuses) near fiscal year-end; avoid repeatedly contacting GMS—if they need anything they will ask. Be patient and monitor eRA Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Just-in-Time (JIT) requests
rubrics_metrics.description: JIT will be requested when ICs are preparing potential awards and need updated items (e.g., other support, certifications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit JIT materials when requested. Do not proactively badger GMS/PO for JIT; if JIT is requested, respond promptly. JIT requests often follow Council consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: When and how to contact the Program Officer (PO)
rubrics_metrics.description: POs can advise on appropriate SRG/study section choices, whether to resubmit (A1), resubmission strategy, and whether to prepare a brief rebuttal, but they often cannot predict funding likelihood before the federal budget is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage PO for strategic advice (e.g., sending Specific Aims for SRG advice, whether to resubmit). Expect limited ability to comment on final funding decisions until IC budget/funding lines are known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission strategy (A1) and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs may be advised to submit an A1 resubmission (e.g., in November) as 'insurance' even if the current application might be funded; ICs generally consider the latest iteration, though some IC policies vary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the summary statement critiques to plan revisions. Ask PO whether to resubmit or focus on improving the existing application; consider submitting to other FOAs/ICs if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing and using a brief rebuttal
rubrics_metrics.description: After receiving the summary statement, ICs may request or accept a short (≈1-page) rebuttal/response to reviewer concerns which is used in internal funding deliberations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a concise rebuttal addressing key critiques if requested by PO; the rebuttal can influence internal IC discussions about funding prioritization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting raw impact scores versus percentiles
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentiles are often more informative than raw impact scores because they show relative standing among peer-reviewed applications; RFAs typically do not have percentiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check percentile when available and compare to IC-specific paylines. Remember percentiles may be misleading for newly formed or recalibrated SRGs; consult PO for interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: IC paylines, interim paylines, and budget uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: Paylines depend on the federal budget. Interim paylines published before a signed budget are conservative; ICs may update paylines retroactively once budgets are finalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor IC interim funding-line policies. Do not assume interim paylines are final; confirm with PO after the summary statement and when budget actions occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiscal year-end effects and continuing resolutions (CRs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Near September 30 ICs may rush to obligate funds; under CRs, most new competing awards may be on hold and only certain award types proceed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect frantic administrative processing at year-end and possible rapid status changes. Be aware that lack of detailed information from PO/GMS during CRs/budget uncertainty is common.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing appropriate study section / SRG assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Use tools like Matchmaker on RePORTER and ART at CSR to generate ranked SRG suggestions; choose SRGs where reviewers read the journals you publish in and attend your conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request SRGs deliberately on submission and tailor Specific Aims and background to the expertise and priorities of the chosen study section. If unsure, ask PO for advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: SRG recalibration, new study sections, and percentile calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: New or reconstituted study sections may 'start fresh' so percentiles can reflect only that meeting; member-conflict or ad hoc panels may calculate percentiles differently or not at all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If assigned to an unfamiliar or member-conflict panel and you are unsure how percentiles are computed, ask the SRO and PO for clarification. Expect score-spreading and recalibration effects in newly formed SRGs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early-Stage Investigator (ESI) status determination
rubrics_metrics.description: ESI status is determined by the end date of clinical training (not by a master's degree); eRA Commons calculates ESI status based on training dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm your ESI status in eRA Commons before requesting ESI-designated benefits or extensions (e.g., COVID-related extensions). If training dates are ambiguous, check with institutional officials or eRA support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion Across the Lifespan (age inclusion) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If excluding participants of certain ages (e.g., children), investigators must justify age-related exclusions/restrictions scientifically or ethically; this justification is usually submitted in the Human Subjects/Inclusion sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear scientific or ethical rationale for any age exclusion; no separate additional narrative beyond existing Human Subjects inclusion justification is usually required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effort adjustment after award (K awards vs R grants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-award reductions in effort are allowed as long as the award's minimum required effort remains met. Dropping below the minimum requires the institution to cover costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before reducing effort, verify the required minimum effort for the activity code and consider clinical status. Coordinate with institutional grants administration if effort changes approach the minimum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-investigator eRA Commons accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-investigators do not necessarily need an eRA Commons account at the exact moment of grant submission; accounts are typically created quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure co-Is create eRA accounts promptly to avoid downstream administrative delays; check with institutional grants office if account creation is delayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to contact CSR Division of Receipt and Referral
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application remains unassigned (no IC or SRG assignment) more than ~2 weeks after submission, CSR may be experiencing delays or may need to be queried.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact CSR Division of Receipt and Referral (phone/email) to confirm receipt and referral status if assignment delays exceed the expected window.

rubrics_metrics.name: How RFAs are evaluated (no percentiles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications to RFAs typically do not receive percentiles; ICs use the impact score, summary statement, and internal priorities to make funding decisions for RFA applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong numeric score on an RFA can be competitive, but funding depends on IC priorities. Consider submitting to non-RFA FOAs concurrently; if awarded via RFA, other submissions will be administratively withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not conflate success rates with payline
rubrics_metrics.description: IC-specific success rates (fraction of applications funded historically) are not equivalent to funding percentiles or paylines for your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using overall success rates to infer whether your percentile is fundable; instead check IC paylines, get PO guidance, and review interim funding policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting project period length and likely award duration
rubrics_metrics.description: You may request a longer project period (e.g., 5 years) even if the IC historically funds fewer years (e.g., NIBIB often awards 4 years for R01s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer writing your proposal for the most likely funded period (based on IC patterns) and consult PO for advice about whether to request 4 vs 5 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applying for administrative supplements (e.g., COVID-19 continuity funding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants do not need explicit PO approval to apply for notices like NOT-OD-20-054 (COVID continuity funding), though PO input is helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If PO is unresponsive, contact higher-level PO management (branch chief or division director) for guidance; do not let lack of PO response prevent submitting a timely supplement request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting to multiple FOAs / diversifying submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: You can submit revised or similar applications to different FOAs or ICs while awaiting an RFA decision; if you receive an award from one mechanism, other active submissions will be administratively withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversify FOAs and SRGs to broaden funding opportunities. Coordinate with PO to avoid jeopardizing active awards and to get advice on targeting appropriate FOAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect administrative variability for small mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Small, uncomplicated awards (e.g., R03) may be processed faster and could transition rapidly from review to award, sometimes skipping intermediate eRA statuses due to heavy GMS workload.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared for quick status changes near fiscal year-end and understand that rapid changes do not necessarily reflect different scientific assessments; avoid excess inquiries during busy processing periods.
